narration: The pipeline takes a point cloud at time t, labelled P sub t, and carries it along the orange loop on the left into the system; the same loop will later return the updated cloud P sub t plus one.
First comes geometry-aware point sampling: eigen feature computation describes the local geometry, a threshold keeps only the informative points, and random sampling thins them to a manageable set.
The sampled points pass to view-based partitioning, where each point's azimuthal angle around the sensor decides which sector of the scene it belongs to.
That angle splits the cloud into four views - front, left, right and rear - so that matching can later be done separately within each direction.
The four views travel down the right-hand connector into feature extraction and matching, where a PointHop plus plus module encodes each point's neighbourhood into a compact descriptor.
Those descriptors drive feature matching in each view, pairing points of the current frame with the previous one inside every sector independently.
The matched correspondences flow left into motion estimation and update, which estimates the rotation and translation between the two frames.
The estimated transform updates the trajectory, the time index advances from t to t plus one, and the cycle repeats with the next point cloud.
